content:
Apple and The King's Trust today announced an expansion of their partnership, launching a new education program that helps young people build creative and digital skills through workshops. Details below.

Apple's partnership with The King's Trust began in 2019.

In a press release today, Apple and The King's Trust announced the 'Apple x King's Trust Creative Labs' program, designed to 'actively help young people explore diverse career paths by connecting with Apple experts from a range of industries, and provide them with the technology, resources, skills, confidence and expertise they need to fulfill their potential.'

Apple said the program's immersive educational experience kicked off earlier this week, featuring 'music industry and creative workshops to mark the opening of the new Apple Music Hall.'

Apple noted that the initial cohort will include up to 20 people aged between 18 and 30, with additional workshops and recruitment to take place over the next year.

Below, Alisha Johnson Wilder, Apple's senior director of Global Community Impact, shares what the program means to Apple and its partnership with The King's Trust:

Jonathan Townsend, UK CEO of The King's Trust, also commented on the program, calling it 'an exciting new chapter in our partnership, which will help even more young people build the confidence and creative digital skills they need to take their next step into employment.'

Apple also said in its announcement that it is working with The King's Trust on resources designed to raise awareness of artificial intelligence and help educators integrate new technologies into their teaching.
